title: Sonochemistry
abstract: Sonochemistry converts acoustic energy into chemical reactivity through acoustic cavitation in liquids. The nucleation, oscillation, growth and collapse of gas–vapour bubbles generate transient hot spots, interfacial reaction zones, shock waves, microstreaming and radical species. This Primer presents the physical basis, experimental implementation and quantitative analysis of sonochemistry by acoustic cavitation. Key aspects include reactor architecture, electrical drive systems, ultrasound transducers, reaction vessels, batch and continuous-flow operation, and the role of frequency, acoustic pressure, gas atmosphere, temperature, solvent properties and geometry. Methods for characterizing cavitation activity and chemical output are discussed, including calorimetry, sonoluminescence imaging and spectroscopy, passive acoustic detection, high-speed imaging, electron paramagnetic resonance spin trapping, and radical dosimetry. Modelling approaches linking ultrasound propagation, bubble dynamics, heat and mass transfer, and chemical kinetics to reactor-scale performance are also considered. Applications in synthesis, catalysis, environmental remediation and materials processing highlight opportunities, whereas standardization, energy efficiency, scale-up and predictive reactor design remain central challenges.
